people.headline: Former Solicitor General of India; global arbitration and constitutional practice
people.short_bio: Harish Salve was designated a Senior Advocate in 1992 and served as Solicitor General of India from 1999 to 2002. He represented India in the Kulbhushan Jadhav case at the International Court of Justice and was appointed King's Counsel for England and Wales in 2020.

people.headline: Former Union Law Minister; multi-time Supreme Court Bar Association President
people.short_bio: Kapil Sibal joined the bar in 1972 and was designated Senior Advocate in 1983. He was appointed Additional Solicitor General of India in 1989, later served as Union Minister of Law and Justice among other cabinet posts, and has been elected President of the Supreme Court Bar Association multiple times, most recently after a landslide win.

positions.title: Union Minister of Law and Justice

people.headline: Senior Advocate and Rajya Sabha MP; among youngest ever designated Senior Advocates
people.short_bio: Abhishek Manu Singhvi is a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India, reported to have been designated at age 34, making him one of the youngest Senior Advocates in the Court's history. He is also a Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha).

notes.body: UNCERTAIN: exact year of Senior Advocate designation not confirmed by a directly retrieved source; commonly reported as occurring at age 34 (circa early 1990s).

people.headline: Former Attorney General for India (2014-2017); high-stakes constitutional and criminal litigation
people.short_bio: Mukul Rohatgi was enrolled as an advocate with the Bar Council of Delhi in May 1978 and designated Senior Advocate by the Delhi High Court in 1994. He served as the 12th Attorney General for India from 19 June 2014 to 18 June 2017 and has also served as Additional Solicitor General of India.

people.headline: Former Solicitor General of India; international arbitration and constitutional law
people.short_bio: Gopal Subramanium was designated a Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court in May 1993, among the youngest to receive the designation. He served as Additional Solicitor General of India (2005-2009) and as Solicitor General of India (2009-2011), and has acted as counsel for major technology and pharmaceutical companies in arbitration and litigation.

people.headline: Constitutional and public law senior advocate; Puttaswamy privacy and Aadhaar cases
people.short_bio: Shyam Divan is a Senior Advocate practising constitutional, civil, banking, securities, arbitration and environmental law at the Supreme Court of India. He appeared in the Justice K.S. Puttaswamy privacy judgment, the Aadhaar challenge, and Navtej Singh Johar decriminalising homosexuality, and is the son of the late Senior Advocate Anil Divan.

people.headline: Senior Advocate; leading authority on tax and constitutional law
people.short_bio: Arvind Datar was designated Senior Advocate by the Madras High Court in 1999 and has over three decades of practice before the Madras High Court and Supreme Court. He authored the biography of Nani Palkhivala and a commentary on the Constitution of India, and appeared in the Vodafone tax case, the National Tax Tribunal case, and the NJAC case. He received the inaugural Fali Nariman Memorial Award in 2025.

people.headline: Senior Advocate; multi-term President of the Supreme Court Bar Association
people.short_bio: Dushyant Dave is a Senior Advocate with over four decades of practice who served as President of the Supreme Court Bar Association across multiple terms, including 2014-15 and again from 2019 until he stepped down on 14 January 2021. He was a member of the National Legal Services Authority from 2004 to 2008.

sources.title: Breaking: Senior Advocate Dushyant Dave elected SCBA President - Bar & Bench

people.headline: Senior Advocate; corporate and high-profile family-business litigation
people.short_bio: C. Aryama Sundaram enrolled with the Madras Bar Council in November 1980 and joined the Chennai firm King & Partridge. He served as Standing Counsel for the Central Government from 1989 and was designated Senior Advocate in 1995 at age 38 -- reportedly the youngest in Madras High Court history at the time -- before relocating his practice to Delhi. He has represented the Mistry family against Tata Sons and the BCCI, among others.

positions.title: Standing Counsel for the Central Government (Madras HC)

people.headline: First woman Senior Advocate (Bombay HC, 1986) and first woman Additional Solicitor General
people.short_bio: Indira Jaising became the first woman designated Senior Advocate, by the Bombay High Court, in 1986, and in 2009 became the first woman appointed Additional Solicitor General of India. She co-founded the NGO Lawyers Collective in 1981 with her husband Anand Grover and has litigated landmark women's rights and workplace sexual harassment cases, and served on the UN CEDAW Committee (2009-2018).

people.headline: Advocate-on-Record known for public interest litigation on corruption and environment
people.short_bio: Prashant Bhushan is an Advocate-on-Record who has practised before the Supreme Court of India since 1983, after studying law at the University of Allahabad. He is known for using public interest litigation on environment, corruption and human rights, and is associated with the Centre for Public Interest Litigation and the People's Union for Civil Liberties.

people.headline: Founder, Human Rights Law Network; Right Livelihood Award laureate (2017)
people.short_bio: Colin Gonsalves is a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India and founder of the Human Rights Law Network (established 1989 in Mumbai), which has grown into a large public-interest legal network. He is senior counsel in the Right to Food case, one of the largest class actions in India, and received the Right Livelihood Award in 2017.

people.headline: First woman Senior Advocate designated on the criminal side by the Delhi High Court
people.short_bio: Rebecca Mammen John enrolled with the Bar Council of Delhi in 1988 and was designated Senior Advocate by the Delhi High Court in 2013, the first woman so designated on the criminal side. She has appeared in high-profile criminal matters including the 1996 hawala case, the Aarushi Talwar murder case, and the Priya Ramani criminal defamation case.

people.headline: Human rights and criminal law advocate; SOAS honorary Doctorate of Laws (2018)
people.short_bio: Vrinda Grover has practised independently as an advocate before the Supreme Court, High Courts and trial courts of India since 1989, specialising in criminal law, women's rights and human rights, representing survivors of communal violence, custodial torture and sexual violence. She holds an LL.M. from New York University School of Law and an LL.B. from Delhi University, and received an honorary Doctorate of Laws from SOAS in 2018.

notes.body: UNCERTAIN: fee band not recorded — no public source states one.

people.headline: Senior Advocate; constitutional, technology and commercial litigation
people.short_bio: Karuna Nundy was designated a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India in 2024. She holds a BA in Economics from St. Stephen's College, Delhi University, an LL.B. from the University of Cambridge, and an LL.M. from Columbia Law School, and was named to Time magazine's 100 most influential people list (2022-2023).

people.headline: Former Additional Solicitor General of India; criminal and white-collar defence
people.short_bio: Sidharth Luthra was admitted to the Bar in Delhi in 1991, completed an LL.B. from Delhi University in 1990 and an MPhil in Criminology from Cambridge in 1991, and was designated Senior Advocate in 2007. He served as Additional Solicitor General of India until his resignation in May 2014, and specialises in criminal law, white-collar crime and cyber fraud.

people.headline: Senior Advocate; civil liberties litigation and Supreme Court amicus roles
people.short_bio: Sanjay Hegde began his career in 1989 with Mulla & Mulla & Craigie Blunt & Caroe, then moved to Delhi to practise in the chambers of Senior Advocate G. Ramaswamy and served for a decade as Advocate-on-Record for the State of Karnataka before focusing on private practice. He was one of two amicus curiae appointed by the Supreme Court in the 2012 Delhi gang-rape case and was appointed an interlocutor in the Shaheen Bagh protests.

people.headline: 16th Attorney General for India (2022-present); constitutional and environmental law
people.short_bio: R. Venkataramani enrolled with the Bar Council of Tamil Nadu in July 1977 and has practised before the Supreme Court for over four decades in constitutional law, environmental law, taxation, and tribal and children's rights. He was appointed the 16th Attorney General for India effective 1 October 2022, succeeding K.K. Venugopal, and his term was extended to 30 September 2027. He served as a Member of the Law Commission of India in 2010 and 2013.

people.headline: Solicitor General of India since 2018; second-longest serving SG after C.K. Daphtary
people.short_bio: Tushar Mehta enrolled as an advocate with the Bar Council of Gujarat in 1987, beginning his career under Senior Advocate Krishnakant Vakharia, and was designated Senior Advocate by the Gujarat High Court in 2008. He was appointed Additional Solicitor General of India in 2014 and has served as Solicitor General of India since 10 October 2018, making him the second-longest serving Solicitor General after C.K. Daphtary.

notes.body: UNCERTAIN: educated at Gujarat University (law degree, five gold medals); no matching institution slug exists in current taxonomy, so education field omitted. Consider adding Gujarat University to _new_institutions.

people.headline: Former Attorney General for India (2017-2022); constitutional law doyen
people.short_bio: Kottayan Katankot Venugopal was enrolled as an advocate on 27 January 1954 and designated Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court of India in 1972. He served as Additional Solicitor General of India in 1979-80 and as the 15th Attorney General for India from 1 July 2017 to 30 September 2022.

people.headline: First woman directly appointed to the Supreme Court from the Bar (2018-2021)
people.short_bio: Indu Malhotra joined the legal profession in 1983 and was designated Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court in 2007, only the second woman to receive that designation. In April 2018 she became the first woman ever directly appointed to the Supreme Court of India from the Bar, and the seventh woman judge of the Court since independence; she retired on 13 March 2021.

people.headline: Senior Advocate; lead counsel in Navtej Singh Johar decriminalising Section 377
people.short_bio: Menaka Guruswamy is a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of India best known, with Arundhati Katju, for successfully arguing Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, which struck down Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code criminalising same-sex relations. She was named to Foreign Policy's '100 Leading Global Thinkers' (2019) and Time magazine's '100 Most Influential People' (2019).

notes.body: UNCERTAIN: one source suggested she became a Rajya Sabha MP in 2026; this personal/political detail was not corroborated further and is omitted from structured fields.

people.headline: Advocate qualified in India and New York; co-counsel in Navtej Singh Johar (Section 377)
people.short_bio: Arundhati Katju is a lawyer qualified to practise in India and New York, best known for representing petitioners with Menaka Guruswamy in Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, the 2018 Supreme Court judgment decriminalising homosexuality in India. She was named to Time magazine's '100 Most Influential People' list in 2019.

people.headline: Additional Solicitor General of India since 2018 (re-appointed multiple terms)
people.short_bio: Vikramjit Banerjee was appointed Additional Solicitor General of India in March 2018 and has been reappointed for subsequent terms. Before litigation, he was on the faculty at the National University of Juridical Sciences (NUJS), and he served as Advocate General of Nagaland from 2015 to 2018.

people.headline: Additional Solicitor General of India; youngest woman ever designated Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court
people.short_bio: Aishwarya Bhati was designated Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court of India in 2019, reportedly the youngest woman ever to receive the designation. She previously served as Additional Advocate General for Uttar Pradesh and is currently an Additional Solicitor General of India -- one of only four women to hold that office -- with a practice focused on women's, children's and disability rights and anti-tobacco litigation.
